chunks: Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Sa'd b. Abdullah narrated to us from al-Qasim b. Muhammad al-Isfahani from Sulayman b. Dawud al-Minqari from Hafs b. Ghiyath. He said: I said to al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad (as):

Inform me about the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, "The month of Ramadan, in which the Quran was revealed" [2:185] — how was the Quran revealed in the month of Ramadan when the Quran was only revealed over a period of twenty years from beginning to end? So he (as) said: The Quran was revealed altogether at once in the month of Ramadan to the Bayt al-Ma'mur. Then, it was revealed from the Bayt al-Ma'mur over a period of twenty years.

key_terms.أنزل: Was sent down — the passive form indicates divine agency in revelation
key_terms.البيت المعمور: The Frequented House — the celestial counterpart of the Ka'ba, located in the fourth heaven according to some reports, where angels worship
key_terms.جملة واحدة: All at once — referring to the complete revelation of the entire Quran as a single unit
key_terms.عز وجل: Mighty and Majestic — a reverential epithet for Allah

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq explain the Quran being revealed in Ramadan when it was revealed over twenty years?
ai.summary: Hafs b. Ghiyath poses a theological question to Imam al-Sadiq about an apparent contradiction in Quran 2:185: how can Ramadan be the month of the Quran's revelation when it was actually revealed over twenty years? The Imam resolves this by explaining that the Quran was first revealed in its entirety to the Bayt al-Ma'mur (the Frequented House in the heavens) during Ramadan, and was then gradually revealed from there to the Prophet over twenty years. This two-stage revelation concept is a significant Shi'i theological teaching.
